liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Feel Like a Stranger** (2 reviews): Bobby flubs the lyrics of the opening song's first verse, which the reviewer finds amusing; Bobby sings wrong verses or words across three consecutive verses of the opener [12][22]
- **Terrapin Station** (1 review): Band returns to Terrapin with a reprise just before Drums [21]

## Setlist highlights

- **mini jam**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [23]
- **terrapin reprise**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]

## The recordings

- **gd83-08-30.senn421.nfagdtrfbyahoo.29342.sbefail.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 21 songs; 152 min; rated 4.22/5 by 9 [1]. Said about its sound: Audience recording has tape hiss and washed-out bass, so it isn't loud and clear; Despite weak bass, this audience tape beats the thin, scratchy soundboard in circulation; Audience tape sounds much better than the soundboard source, which has distracting cuts and edits [16][17][19]
- **gd1983-08-30.148764.fob.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 19 songs; 156 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd1983-08-30.111590.senn.daweez.d5scott.flac16**: source not stated; 19 songs; 151 min; rated 4.17/5 by 6 [6]. Said about its sound: Reviewer judges this the best source for the show, better than the soundboard [21]
- **gd83-08-30.sbd.dodd.15110.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 18 songs; 136 min; rated 3.2/5 by 5 [9]

## Around the show

- Reviewer prefers 1983 Dead to the 1970s, citing nastier Jerry tone, harder rocking, and heavy Hammond organ from Brent [14]
- Reviewer says 1980s Dead were harder rocking and bluesier than the 1970s, thanks to Bobby's blues songs and Brent's voice and Hammond [18]
- Reviewer calls this a distinctively bluesy Dead show, with lyric mistakes here and there [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd83-08-30.senn421.nfagdtrfbyahoo.29342.sbefail.flac16**: source: Sennheiser 421's > Sony TC-D5 [1]. Also: Recorded with Sennheiser 421 microphones into a Sony TC-D5; transfer used a first-generation cassette copy; Cassette went through a Sony TC-D5M, Soundblaster, Soundforge and CD-Wave to FLAC; seeded by nfagdtrfbyahoo [1]
- **gd1983-08-30.148764.fob.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Mark Severson; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Mark Severson's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; 3 x Nakamichi 700 mics (left and right cardioid, center omni, row R, seat 208, DFC) > Jamie Pouris' custom… [2]. Also: An eight-second patch in Drums comes from Otto Rice's Sennheiser 421 front-of-board source [2]
- **gd1983-08-30.111590.senn.daweez.d5scott.flac16**: taped by Da Weez; transferred by D5scott; source: Source: 2 Sennheiser 441 microphones > Sony TC-D5M - analog master cassettes; [6]
- **gd83-08-30.sbd.dodd.15110.sbeok.shnf**: source: MSC>Cass. x 2>PCM>DAT>CDR Set Ip + Set II: Kesey's MSC>DAT>CDR Audience patches: Sennheiser 421's>Sony TC-D5M>Cass.>DAT>CDR taped by Rick Saeger(previous seed) [9]. Also: Soundboard transfer carries audience patches taped by Rick Saeger with Sennheiser 421s via cassette and DAT [9]

- Poster by Kathleen Elizabeth Fowler Grateful: [1983-08-29 Silva Hall, Hult Center, Eugene, OR, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1983-08-29-silva-hall-hult-center-eugene-or-usa/) [24]
